title: He Married a Prostitute… Because God Told Him To
paragraphs:
He Married a Prostitute… Because God Told Him To
The Scandal That Revealed the Heart of God Like Nothing Else Ever Could
You wouldn’t expect God to ask something like this.
Not from a holy God. Not from a righteous God. Not from a God who commands purity, faithfulness, and covenant loyalty.
Yet there it is… raw, uncomfortable, impossible to ignore.
In the opening lines of the book of Hosea, God doesn’t just speak a message… He becomes the message through a man.
The Hebrew hits harder than the English ever could.

"וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֶל־הוֹשֵׁעַ לֵךְ קַח־לְךָ אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים וְיַלְדֵי זְנוּנִים..."
Vayomer YHWH el-Hoshea: Lech kach-lecha eshet zenunim v’yaldei zenunim…
“The LORD said to Hosea, ‘Go, take for yourself a wife of whoredom and children of whoredom…’” (Hosea 1:2)
No metaphor. No softening. No explanation first.
Just a command that feels… wrong.
Before you understand it, before you justify it, before your theology can catch up…
God tells His prophet to step into a scandal.
And everyone knew what she was.
This wasn’t a hidden past. This wasn’t a quiet mistake.
Can you imagine the silence after that command?
The questions he didn’t dare say out loud…
“God… You want me to represent You… by marrying her?”
Because Hosea wasn’t just being asked to love a broken woman.
He was being called to feel what God feels.
Running after other gods, other desires, other loves.
The Hebrew word used—zenunim—doesn’t just mean physical immorality. It carries the weight of faithlessness, of covenant betrayal, of a heart that keeps leaving even after being chosen.
“This is what My people are like.”
Instead of rewriting them out of the story…
He writes Himself into their mess.
And for a moment… maybe it feels like it could work.
But sin doesn’t disappear just because love shows up.
And this is where most people would close the story.
Because this is where human love reaches its limit.

“לֵךְ עוֹד אֱהַב אִשָּׁה…”
Lech od, ehav ishah…
“Go again, love a woman…” (Hosea 3:1)
Do you feel how unreasonable that is?
How offensive that is to human pride?
How impossible that is to do without God?
Not as a man chasing romance.
But as a man carrying the weight of divine love.
He doesn’t say, “You made your choice.”

"וָאֶכְּרֶהָ לִּי..."
Va’ekreha li…
“So I bought her for myself…” (Hosea 3:2)
He buys back his own wife.
The one who broke the covenant…
But because love refused to let her stay lost.
This is not just Hosea’s story.
This is the Gospel before the Gospel had a name.
And He wouldn’t just marry a broken people…
The Greek in the New Testament captures it with piercing clarity:

“ἔτι ἁμαρτωλῶν ὄντων ἡμῶν…”
Eti hamartōlōn ontōn hēmōn…
“While we were still sinners…” (Romans 5:8)
Not after you cleaned your life.
Not after you proved your loyalty.
Do you understand what that means?
God didn’t wait for your faithfulness.
He loved you in your unfaithfulness.
He didn’t choose you because you were worthy.
He made you worthy by choosing you.
And if that doesn’t break something inside you…
You haven’t really seen it yet.
Because this story forces a question most people avoid:
If God loves like this… why do we run like that?
Why do we still chase things that leave us empty?
Why do we still trade eternity for moments?
Why do we still act like Gomer… knowing there’s a Hosea waiting?
This hit harder than you expected.
Because somewhere deep down… you recognize yourself in her.
The moments you knew better… but did it anyway.
Still being pursued by a love that refuses to quit.
So what do you do with that?
And someone you know needs this.
That family member who feels too far gone.
That person who thinks God could never want them back.
And if you feel something stirring… don’t ignore it.
Stay close to the kind of words that don’t just inform you… they transform you.
And if you’re serious about growing deeper in Jesus Christ… there’s more waiting for you.
Because if God gave everything to redeem you…
Is it really too much to support what’s helping others find Him?
And right now… you have a choice.
Or step into the kind of love that rewrites everything.
Because the same God who told Hosea to go back…
And somehow… even now… after everything… He still calls you His.
